question:
A 29-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious in a park.
He appears disheveled and emits a strong odor of alcohol. His medical history includes prior treatment
for alcohol withdrawal at this hospital. The patient exhibits altered mental status, occasionally muttering
incomprehensible words. Vital signs include a heart rate of 94/min, blood pressure of 117/66 mm Hg,
respiratory rate of 20/min, and temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). Physical examination reveals no
significant abnormalities, with clear lung sounds, a soft abdomen, and no rashes. Initial laboratory
findings are as follows: | Blood glucose | 56 mg/dL | | --- | --- | | Blood alcohol level | 215 mg/dL | |
Hemoglobin | 10.9 g/dL | | WBCs | 10,000/mm³ | | Platelets | 145,000/mm³ | | Lactate level | 2.2 mmol/L
| What is the most likely explanation for this patient’s hypoglycemia? Answer Choices: (A) Suppression
of counter-regulatory hormones (B) Direct inhibition of glucose-6-phosphatase by ethanol (C) Glycogen
depletion (D) A decrease in the ratio of the reduced form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide to
nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH/NAD+) ratio (E) Alcohol-induced pancreatic β-cell
dysfunction (F) Increased insulin sensitivity from chronic alcohol use (G) Enhanced peripheral glucose
utilization (H) Alcohol dehydrogenase–induced diuresis (I) Impaired gluconeogenesis due to elevated
acetaldehyde levels (J) Decreased hepatic glucose output due to mitochondrial dysfunction
 A. A decrease in the ratio of the reduced form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide to nicotinamide
adenine dinucleotide (NADH/NAD+) ratio
B. Alcohol-induced pancreatic β-cell dysfunction
C. Alcohol dehydrogenase–induced diuresis
D. Decreased hepatic glucose output due to mitochondrial dysfunction
E. Direct inhibition of glucose-6-phosphatase by ethanol
F. Enhanced peripheral glucose utilization
G. Suppression of counter-regulatory hormones
H. Increased insulin sensitivity from chronic alcohol use
I. Glycogen depletion

J. Impaired gluconeogenesis due to elevated acetaldehyde levels
